text:
Good morning. It is Sunday, October twenty-fifth, six-thirty in the morning.

First, the news from home.

Story one. The National Democratic Congress has held its constituency executive elections across the country, but the process faced pockets of unrest, arrests, and protests. Joy Online, Three News, and The Ghana Report inform us that police arrested delegates in Bimbilla and Wa Central for photographing their ballots, while in the Ashanti Region, delegates in Atwima Kwanwoma invoked curses over a missing names register, and aspirants in Oforikrom protested missing ballot papers. However, Three News notes that the Western Regional Minister described voting across all seventeen constituencies in his region as peaceful, and Joy Online reported that all twenty-four executive posts in Juaboso went entirely uncontested.

Story two. The flagbearer of the New Patriotic Party, Doctor Mahamudu Bawumia, has continued his nationwide stakeholder consultations by meeting with the Pharmaceutical Society of Ghana in Accra. Graphic Online says the leadership shared proposals with him on how to expand local drug manufacturing and establish Ghana as the foremost pharmaceutical hub in the West African subregion.

Story three. The newly elected National Nasara Organizer of the New Patriotic Party, Alhaji Ali Suraj, has declared that his party successfully transformed politics in Zongo communities from neglect into empowerment. The Ghana Report informs us that he highlighted interventions such as the Zongo Development Fund and financial backing for youth pursuing tertiary education as evidence of that progress.

Now, around the world.

Story four. Protests over the rising cost of living brought hundreds of thousands of people into the streets of France, with demonstrations also spreading into neighbouring European nations. The B B C and France Twenty-Four report that nearly one thousand people were arrested across France after peaceful daytime marches in Paris and other cities gave way to nightfall clashes with riot police firing tear gas.

Story five. In the Middle East, tensions have surged ahead of Israel's national election following the demolition of Palestinian homes by Israeli security forces in the West Bank city of Hebron. France Twenty-Four and the B B C report that the action has displaced about twelve hundred residents, coming shortly after two Israeli soldiers were killed on Friday and as thousands of citizens marched in Tel Aviv protesting against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

You can open Dad News and ask for more about any story by its number.
